jobs.description: The opportunity At Unity, we don't just help game developers build their games: we help them grow what they've built, and get their titles in front of the right players, through an ad system that makes billions of real-time decisions every day. Getting that right at this scale is a permanent engineering problem. It belongs to our Ads Privacy team, which owns privacy compliance alongside the creative moderation and fraud prevention systems that keep the network trustworthy. You will own privacy-critical services end to end, from design through production. You will work in the request path, where a wrong answer is both a legal exposure and a revenue event. CTS, CTS-I, manufacturer certifications, low-voltage training, OSHA 10, or other AV-related credentials. jobs.description: Job Description Summary: The Coca-Cola Company is seeking a Director, Data Architect for Global Equipment Platforms (GEP). GEP is building the next generation of connected equipment capabilities across Freestyle, dispensed, coolers, digital racks, IoT-enabled assets, and future equipment ecosystems. As GEP evolves from individual equipment platforms into a connected commercial network, data architecture will be critical to enabling scalable analytics, AI, predictive maintenance, beverage quality intelligence, operational visibility, and customer-facing data products. The Director, Data Architect will define and govern the enterprise data architecture for GEP. This role establishes the data models, data contracts, architecture patterns, governance standards, and data product foundations needed to support telemetry, equipment data, service data, product analytics, and AI-ready capabilities across the global equipment ecosystem. This is a senior individual contributor architecture leadership role responsible for defining GEP's data architecture vision, standards, and federated operating model. The role will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Unified IoT, Platform, Data Science, Operating Units, Bottlers, Legal, Security, and external partners, while working within the broader enterprise and global data architecture framework to ensure GEP's data ecosystem is scalable, governed, discoverable, reusable, and aligned to enterprise technology standards and business priorities. Key Responsibilities: Define GEP’s Enterprise Data Architecture Evaluate existing data architecture, platforms, and capabilities across GEP and the broader enterprise ecosystem; identify gaps and opportunities; and define a target-state architecture and modernization roadmap aligned to enterprise standards, business priorities, and future-state digital and AI capabilities. Lead the definition of GEP’s enterprise data architecture across equipment telemetry, operational events, service data, product analytics, customer-facing insights, and AI/ML use cases. Establish canonical data models for core entities such as equipment, devices, outlets, customers, bottlers, telemetry events, service events, products, consumption, configurations, and operational states. Define architecture patterns for how data flows across source systems, Unified IoT, KOS, FOS, Microsoft Fabric, Data Hub, APIs, data products, and downstream applications. Partner with GEP Engineering, Platform, Unified IoT, and broader global architecture and technology teams to ensure data architecture standards are implementable, scalable, secure, and operationally sustainable. Own Data Contracts and Semantic Consistency Define and govern data contracts between source systems, OEMs, vendors, platform teams, and data consumers. Establish standards for schemas, metadata, lineage, naming conventions, data definitions, and semantic layers. Establish and evolve business ontologies and knowledge models that define the relationships between equipment, telemetry, products, customers, service events, and operational processes, enabling consistent data interpretation, interoperability, discoverability, and AI-ready capabilities. Ensure data generated by equipment and upstream systems can be consistently understood, reused, governed, and consumed across analytics, AI, reporting, and product workflows. Partner with Unified IoT and Common Equipment Data Language efforts to ensure telemetry and equipment data are aligned to enterprise-level definitions. Enable Data Products at Scale Define architectural standards for reusable data products, including curated datasets, APIs, semantic models, feature layers, and governed access patterns. Support the shift from ad hoc analytics and fragmented reporting toward scalable, reusable data products that answer business questions end to end. Ensure data products are designed for multiple stakeholder personas, including product teams, engineering teams, operations, operating units, bottlers, account teams, and future customer-facing use cases. Partner with Data Product, Analytics, and Data Science teams to ensure data products are production-grade, measurable, documented, and governed. Scale is building AI for the world's most important decisions. From the front lines of national defense to the core of global enterprise, we provide the data engine and agentic infrastructure that powers the next generation of American and allied interests.
As a Deployment Strategist supporting Space Systems Command (SSC), you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and mission-critical production in the space domain. You will lead the charge in deploying Agentic AI — autonomous, reasoning systems — into space operations workflows, from space domain awareness to ground segment modernization to tasking and targeting.
The Role
We are looking for an executive account leader who understands that winning at SSC isn't about a successful 6-month OTA prototype; it's about Program of Record integration. You will focus on landing and transitioning high-stakes prototypes into full-scale deployments across SSC's Program Executive Offices, navigating the Valley of Death by securing executive sponsorship and programmed funding.
This is an expansion role in a high-opportunity segment. Scale has significant USAF work and space-adjacent programs; your mandate is to convert that into core Space Force business.
Responsibilities
This is an individual contributor role with heavy leadership expectations. You are the "CEO of the Account," responsible for the following:
Full-Spectrum Capture & Quota Ownership:
Carry and exceed a multi-million dollar annual revenue quota. You own the entire lifecycle: identifying top-of-funnel opportunity, shaping requirements, and driving to contract award and revenue recognition.
Tactical Execution:
You don't just delegate; you execute. You will personally draft white papers and SBIR/OTA responses, lead complex proposal development, architect deal structures, and navigate the nuances of space acquisition.
Operational Transition:
Once the deal is signed, your job isn't over. You will continue to lead the account, ensuring the delivery team (Engagement Managers, Technical PMs, Engineers, and Product) enables mission success. You are the primary point of contact, ensuring the pilot doesn't just work, but scales.
Renewal, Expansion & Growth:
Own the long-term account strategy across SSC's PEOs. Identify the next use case, secure follow-on funding, and drive the growth that turns a single deployment into an enterprise standard.
Direct Agentic Solutioning:
Work in the weeds with technical teams and operators to co-design Agentic AI workflows. You must be able to translate a Guardian's mission problem into a specific technical requirement our engineers can build against.
SI & Prime Orchestration:
In partnership with Scale's Partner Managers, actively manage and negotiate with Tier 1 Systems Integrators and space primes to ensure Scale is the agentic AI engine inside their larger programs. You will be the lead negotiator on subcontracting and teaming agreements.
Requirements
Experience:
7+ years across space operations, government acquisitions, complex enterprise IT sales, or defense business development. Time in uniform in the Space Force, or in Air Force space, counts heavily here.
Proven Track Record:
You have closed and implemented multi-year deals and know how to get a line item into the budget.
Domain Expertise:
Deep understanding of Space Force modernization priorities — space domain awareness, ground and command-and-control modernization, resilient architectures — and where AI/ML, computer vision, and autonomy apply.
The Valley of Death Navigator:
Demonstrated ability to move technology from "cool demo" to "deployed capability" inside a major PEO or program office.
Strategic Network:
Existing relationships across SSC and the broader Space Force enterprise, plus a Rolodex at the major space primes and integrators.
Clearance:
Active Secret clearance required; TS/SCI strongly preferred.
Education:
BS/BA required; technical degree or MBA preferred.
Geography:
Based in the Los Angeles area, with the ability to work on-site or with the customer 3 days a week. Proximity to SSC at Los Angeles AFB is essential to this role.
Travel:
Ability to travel 20-30% of the time.
Who You Are
Mission-Driven:
You believe whoever wins in AI wins the next century, and you want that to be the United States and its allies.
Relentless:
You thrive in the long game of defense procurement. Bureaucracy doesn't discourage you; you see it as a puzzle to be solved.
Adaptive:
You can operate in the high-velocity environment of a Series E startup while maintaining the polish required in front of a general officer.
The Closer-Operator:
You have the executive presence to brief a PEO and the tactical stamina to spend 10 hours in a SCIF on a proposal response.
Radically Accountable:
You don't wait for a marketing lead or a BD specialist to hand you a deal. You build your own funnel, navigate the "no's," and find the creative path to "yes."
Technically Credible:
You aren't a software engineer, but you can explain the difference between RAG and agentic reasoning to a skeptical technical evaluator.

Scopely is looking for a smart, technically strong, and process-adaptive
Senior QA
to join our Royal Lounge Casino team in Bangalore on a hybrid basis
.
At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play, every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues, or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.
With 30M+ downloads, Grand Casino is home to slots, bingo, cards, and more! Team members are distributed across the globe with hubs in Bengaluru, Tel Aviv, Barcelona, among others
What You’ll Do
Write, maintain, and execute test cases for studio games across mobile and web platforms, covering a broad range of devices, operating systems, and browsers.
Perform functional and non-functional testing of mobile applications, including network traffic, API responses, and log analysis.
Collaborate closely with Scrum teams, Producers, Developers, and QA Leads/Managers to ensure releases meet high quality standards.
Communicate proactively with Developers and business stakeholders during defect triage to reduce defect ageing and drive timely resolution.
Conduct root cause analysis for defects and provide corrective and preventive action plans.
Work effectively in an Agile environment to support timely and high-quality product delivery.
Identify quality trade-offs, project risks, and appropriate mitigation strategies.
Develop a detailed understanding of studio games, including gameplay flows, player journeys, edge cases, and game-specific scenarios.
Create and maintain QA documentation, including test cases, test plans, test reports, training material, and process documentation.
Mentor junior QA team members and support their technical and domain growth.
Partner with the QA Lead to continuously improve QA processes, test coverage, and release quality.
Support team coordination and delivery in the absence of the QA Lead.
What We're Looking For
4–7 years of experience in software testing, preferably across mobile, web, or gaming products.
Strong familiarity with mobile and web platforms from a QA perspective.
Good understanding of client-server architecture, APIs, application data flow, and network debugging.
Hands-on experience in test design, test execution, defect reporting, regression testing, and risk-based testing.
Strong exploratory testing skills, with the ability to select the right test approach based on feature complexity and risk.
Experience using QA tools such as Jira, TestRail, Charles Proxy, Fiddler, browser developer tools, or similar tools.
Ability to create clear and comprehensive QA documentation, including test cases, test plans, test reports, and training material.
Good understanding of software testing processes, SDLC/STLC, and Agile methodologies.
Basic knowledge of SQL and database concepts.
Strong communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Bonus Points
Experience testing mobile games, web games, or live-service products.
Passion for gaming, with a genuine interest in playing and understanding casual games.
Strong gaming mindset, including an understanding of player behaviour, engagement mechanics, progression, rewards, and LiveOps.
Prior experience testing Slots, Casino, or other real-money/social casino-style games.
Exposure to test automation frameworks and AI-driven testing approaches.
About Scopely
Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.
Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.
Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.
Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit:

jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI's Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) team partners across the company to enable safe, responsible growth. This role will be a senior EHS partner to our robotics operations as our operating footprint expands. You will work closely with Robotics, Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Workplace, Construction, Security, People, Legal, and external partners to integrate safety into how our facilities are designed, built, staffed, and operated. About the Role We are seeking a Senior Manager, EHS - Robotics to provide senior, hands-on safety leadership across multiple sites. This role is for an experienced EHS leader who can operate independently in a fast-moving technical environment, anticipate risk before it becomes an incident, and build practical safety systems that scale with the business. Our robotics operations are scaling quickly, with a growing mix of construction, commissioning, workforce expansion, and around-the-clock operations. This creates a complex and evolving risk environment and requires strong preventive planning, consistent field presence, and sustained incident-management oversight. This leader will own site-level EHS strategy and execution for the robotics portfolio while partnering with the broader EHS team on company-wide standards and programs. The successful candidate will look around corners: planning for future ramps, identifying requirements early, influencing design and operating decisions, and creating durable systems that enable teams to move quickly without compromising safety. In this role you will: - Serve as a senior EHS partner across robotics R&D operations, owning site-level safety strategy, priorities, and execution as the footprint scales. - Anticipate EHS requirements for new operations, equipment, processes, construction phases, staffing ramps, and 24/7 operations, and translate them into practical plans before work begins. - Lead proactive risk identification and control across robotics activities, including machine safety, ergonomics, electrical safety, material handling, hazardous materials, contractor safety, and other site-specific risks. - Build and maintain site EHS programs, risk assessments, procedures, training, inspections, corrective-action systems, emergency preparedness, and compliance processes appropriate to each site's risk profile. - Partner with Robotics, Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Workplace, Construction, Security, People, Legal, and vendors to embed safety into facility design, equipment deployment, work planning, and operating decisions. - Provide visible field leadership across shifts and operating conditions, establishing mechanisms that support effective EHS coverage and escalation for 24/7 operations. - Lead incident response and investigation for significant events; ensure timely fact-finding, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, verification, trend analysis, and communication of lessons learned. - Use incident, near-miss, inspection, and operational data to identify recurring risks and drive preventive actions across sites rather than addressing events in isolation. - Oversee contractor and contingent-worker safety interfaces, clarifying responsibilities, expectations, reporting, and corrective-action ownership across multi-employer worksites. - Maintain strong regulatory compliance and readiness, including applicable Cal/OSHA and OSHA requirements, while developing metrics and reporting that make site risks, actions, and performance visible to leadership. You’ll thrive in this role if you have: - 15+ years of progressive EHS experience, including significant leadership responsibility in robotics, advanced manufacturing, R&D, industrial, or similarly complex technical environments. - Strong technical knowledge across occupational safety and health, with depth in areas such as machine safety, ergonomics, electrical safety, hazardous energy, material handling, hazardous materials, contractor safety, and incident investigation. - Demonstrated experience supporting complex sites through rapid scale, construction and operational overlap, commissioning, process change, or transition to extended or 24/7 operations. - Strong working knowledge of OSHA and Cal/OSHA requirements and the ability to translate regulatory obligations into practical, scalable operating programs. - Demonstrated success influencing senior technical and operational leaders, especially where EHS does not directly own the work and decisions must be made through partnership. - Experience building EHS systems, programs, metrics, vendor support, and operating rhythms for an emerging or rapidly scaling organization. - Strong judgment and the ability to balance operational speed, technical complexity, workforce needs, compliance, and risk without defaulting to overly rigid solutions. - Clear, credible communication skills with executives, engineers, operators, contractors, employees, and external partners, including the ability to communicate during high-pressure incidents. - Comfort operating independently in ambiguity, with the technical depth, field orientation, pragmatism, and ownership needed to anticipate what is coming and build durable safety capability ahead of growth.
